articles.title: Oregon school shooter identified as 16-year-old former student
articles.summary: A teacher and one of the three children who were killed in Thursday's mass shooting at a Bend, Ore., elementary school were identified on Friday during a press conference in which authorities provided additional details about the incident. The 16-year-old suspect, who was killed by a community member within minutes of opening fire at the school, was also identified. Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said Friday that Rhoam Summer, a 5-year-old student, and Meghan Lambert, a 25-year-old teacher, were among the four victims in a special education classroom at Silver Rail Elementary School. In a statement, Lambert's family described her as a native central Oregonian who grew up in Bend and had a passion for playing sports, especially volleyball. "Her goal was to be an educator and teach in the school district she loved growing up in," the statement continued.  "Silver Rail was her first job as a teacher. … She loved Silver Rail. This was her dream job. Meghan was compassionate and had a huge heart. She always fought for the underdog and those with special needs. She was an incredible sister, daughter, niece and granddaughter. … She was funny and opinionated and she lit up the room." Community members grieve at the site of a makeshift memorial in front of Silver Rail Elementary School. Mathieu Lewis-Rolland via Getty Images The shooter was identified as Griffin John II. He was a former student at the school who had received special ed services, according to Bend-La Pine School Superintendent Steven Cook. The names of the two other victims, who were 8 and 11 years old, have not been made public. A 7-year-old student and a teacher were hospitalized with critical injuries after the incident. The child, who has not been identified, is in "serious, but stable, condition," Krantz said. The wounded teacher was identified by the AP as Becky Drury, an educational assistant at Silver Rail Elementary. According to a Facebook post from her mother-in-law, Drury has already had surgery to repair significant damage to her left arm and will need more surgeries in the future. She also suffered injuries to her right hand, but none of her wounds are believed to be life-threatening. "The good news is she will be ok and we all get to keep that magnificent woman we love so much in our lives," the post read. Police declined to confirm the name of the bystander who killed John, but he had previously been identified by the Associated Press as Kyle Giamanco, a lifelong Bend resident and the father of two young daughters at the school. "He is not seeking recognition, but instead wishes to express his gratitude to the first responders, school personnel and community for the outpouring of love and support," Giamanco's mother, Kenda Freeman, said while reading a prepared statement to reporters outside her son's home near the school. "I don't think we can underestimate or underappreciate [his] courage," Krantz said Friday, referring to Giamanco's decision to intervene. "When someone is willing to risk their own life for others, we recognize that. And the quick thinking to … follow someone into the school is incredible, and undoubtedly saved people." Other than John's past association with the school, police did not share any information on the potential motive behind the shooting. "Everyone wants to know why, including us," Krantz said. "We may never get that full answer, but we want it." Krantz said John used a Maverick 88 12-gauge pump-action shotgun in the shooting. He declined to comment on where he acquired the gun. How the shooting unfolded Flowers are placed beside a sign at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Ore., on Friday. AP Photo/Haven Daley Krantz provided new details about what happened in the chaotic few minutes from when John first opened fire outside the school to when he was killed. According to Krantz, John approached the school at approximately 12:58 p.m. on foot before throwing his gun over an exterior fence and climbing onto the school's property. A driver in a red pickup truck spotted John and "verbally confronted" him from inside their vehicle. John fired at least three rounds at the truck before heading inside. The driver, who was unhurt, quickly called 911 to alert police. John then walked around the outside of the school and fired multiple rounds into the glass panes of an exterior door to gain access to the school. He then turned left into a special education classroom and immediately began firing. In total, John fired as many as 15 rounds, Krantz said. Giamanco, who had seen John fire at the pickup truck, parked his car in the school parking lot, grabbed his pistol and began following John's path into the school. As he entered through the shot-out doors, Giamanco found a teacher involved in a physical altercation with John. He fired several rounds from his pistol, striking John multiple times. Officers arrived at the scene within three minutes of the first 911 call. "Seconds later, officers reported the suspect had been shot and killed, possibly by a bystander," police wrote in an incident report on Thursday. Officers then cleared the school, and all students and staff were transported to a nearby church for reunification with families and guardians. According to Krantz, John was carrying an additional 44 rounds of ammunition when he was killed. No other students other than the three who were killed and the one who was injured were in the classroom at the time, Krantz said. There was no School Resource Officer present at the school. 'They're babies' People leave a family reunification area following a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Ore., on Thursday. AP Photo/Joe Kline Witnesses described hearing gunshots and seeing police swarm the school. "I heard what I thought was gunshots," Erin Johnson, who was visiting her parents next door to the school, told Oregon Public Broadcasting on Thursday. "Then my neighbor began to scream shortly thereafter — her kids go to school there, at Silver Rail. Then I heard the police coming in." She added: "It's heartbreaking. I don't know any details right now about who was injured. But they're babies." Krista Johnson told OregonLive that she saw police swarm the school. "So many people stopping what they were doing," she said Thursday. "I knew that something had happened." Angela Nuchols told the Bend Source that she and her husband had dressed their 8-year-old daughter up for picture day before school, then raced to Silver Rail after hearing about the shooting. "It was crawling with police officers from all over the county," she said. "You've got guys in tactical gear, rifles. You're just scared to death wondering, is your child okay? You don't know." They were later reunited with their daughter. "It was like the worst three hours of our lives," Nuchols said. Thousands attended a vigil at Bend's Drake Park on Thursday night, many carrying candles, flowers and stuffed toys. "There is power and love in this park tonight," Kotek said at the vigil, according to OregonLive. "On behalf of everyone who lives in Oregon, I am so sorry for what you are experiencing today. No parent, no family, no community should have to have this kind of day." Free counseling is being offered to anyone in the community who may need help dealing the emotional weight of the tragedy. As of Friday afternoon, close to 200 people had already utilized those services, according to Deschutes County Health Services Director Mary Harris. The Bend Education Association, which represents 1,000 educators in the city, released a statement emphasizing the work that will be needed to ensure that every student and teacher affected by the shooting has the support that they need. "When violence happens in one of our schools, it reaches far beyond that building," the group's president, Sarah Barclay, wrote on social media. "It affects our families, our colleagues, and communities across our country. Every student and every person who works in our schools deserves to be safe." articles.title: A teacher saved lives by tackling and fighting the Oregon shooter, police say
articles.summary: By Herbert Villarraga and Deborah Bloom BEND, Oregon, Oct 16 (Reuters) - A teacher in the Oregon classroom where a shooter killed three children and an adult threw her cellphone at the shooter, tackled him and fought him in an act that saved lives, police said on Friday. A day ‌into their investigation of the latest U.S. school shooting, authorities released new details of the scene inside a special needs classroom of Silver Rail ‌Elementary School where three school children aged 5, 8 and 11 and a teacher were killed by a 16-year-old former student. Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz did not identify the teacher who fought the assailant, ​but told a press conference she threw her cell phone at the suspect, tackled him and fought to take his shotgun from him. "She was not injured in that incident, but she almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed," Krantz said. As the two wrestled, a parent entered the classroom and opened fire on the gunman, killing him. Officials said the parent had followed the shooter into the school, upon witnessing him firing a shotgun from just outside campus. By the time police arrived within three minutes of receiving their first call, the shooter ‌was dead, police said. In the meantime the 16-year-old assailant, who ⁠had shot through locked glass doors to enter campus, had killed four people and wounded two others. Krantz, speaking to the heroism shown by the teacher who threw herself onto the suspect and the parent who shot him, said, "I don't think we can underestimate ⁠or under-appreciate that courage. When someone is willing to risk their own life for others, we recognize that." He said that the bystander's actions "undoubtedly saved people," and "the teacher who was willing to stand and fight for her children, that's true heroism." Krantz identified the shooter as Griffin J. John II, who was armed with 12-gauge shotgun. He fired about 15 rounds in the classroom ​and ​had another 44 rounds on him. The parent who killed the shooter was identified as Kaylub Giamanco, his mother ​told the New York Times. She identified him as the ‌father of two girls who attend the school, according to video posted by the New York Times of Freeman reading a brief statement. "He is not seeking recognition, but instead wishes to express his gratitude to the first responders, school personnel, and community for the outpouring of love and support," Freeman said. "Kaylub's family, including his two daughters who attend the school, respectfully asks for privacy during this difficult time, and will not be participating in interviews at this time." Residents of Bend, a city of about 100,000 people some 175 miles (280 km) southeast of Portland, gathered near the school to mourn on Friday morning, placing flowers and candles just outside yellow crime scene tape that cordoned off the ‌scene. "Thank God for that father. He saved a lot of lives yesterday, and our prayers should ​go out for him because he has a lot on his mind today. We wish him well, ​and thank God for him," Michael Zappa, 71, who lives just blocks ​from the school, said through tears. Brooke Olsen, the mother of a kindergartener who was safely reunited with her family after the shooting, ‌also expressed gratitude for the man who stopped the shooter. "This is ​an extremely painful day of grief for ​everybody in Bend, especially Silver Rail families, and we have to think about what's next for safety measures." Such school shootings have become common in the US, with each one reviving debates over gun laws in a country where a right to "keep and bear Arms" is protected under the Constitution's Second Amendment. Some ​of the deadliest school attacks in the US include those ‌at Columbine High School in 1999, Sandy Hook Elementary School in 2012, Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in 2018 and Robb Elementary School in ​Uvalde, Texas, in 2022. (Reporting by Herbert Villarraga and Deborah Bloom in Bend; Additional reproting by Jonathan Allen in New York and Steve Gorman ​in Los Angeles; Writing by Daniel Trotta; Editing by Paul Thomasch and Jonathan Spicer) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/teacher-tackled-fought-oregon-school-221156030.html

articles.title: Katie Zacharia reportedly out as White House press secretary after first week on the job
articles.summary: President Trump signaled on Friday that he might replace embattled new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia after less than one week on the job. Around the same time, multiple outlets reported that Zacharia had already been let go. Citing "three people familiar with the matter," the New York Times reported on Friday afternoon that Trump had "fired" Zacharia. A senior White House official told Fox News that Zacharia is "transitioning out" of her role, and CBS News, Politico and the Washington Post published similar reports. If confirmed, that would make Zacharia the shortest-tenured White House press secretary in U.S. history. "We're talking about doing something," Trump told reporters outside the White House, adding that he told Zacharia to "reconsider" whether she "need[s] this." "I told her, 'I think you're better off being happy and I don't think you could ever be happy in this job,'" Trump said. Asked if he was planning to "fire" Zacharia, the president said no. But, he added, "I want her to have a good life. I don't want [her] to have a life like she's led in the last three days. She is being brutalized by the media." Trump: "I told Katie that in my opinion she was treated very very unfairly by the news. Let's call it the fake news. I said, 'Katie, do you need this? I don't think you need this.' We're talking about doing something. I want her to have a good life. She's being brutalized by the… pic.twitter.com/Ivkk5imCjS — Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) October 16, 2026 Trump said he would discuss the matter further with Zacharia when he returns from a Friday campaign rally in Georgia. The president announced on Friday, Oct. 9, that he had chosen Zacharia, a conservative commentator and former Department of Homeland Security spokesperson, to replace Karoline Leavitt, who left the administration in August. Zacharia started at the White House on Monday gave her first press briefing on Tuesday. But she has spent the days since then facing questions about her own legal credentials rather than Trump's agenda. In his post on Truth Social announcing her appointment, Trump described Zacharia as an "attorney" as well as "a devoted fan and member of MAGA!" Zacharia holds both a law degree and a bachelor's degree from Pepperdine University, and her LinkedIn page says she served as "general counsel" at Fix California, a nonprofit founded by former acting Kennedy Center director Ric Grenell to promote conservative policies in the Golden State. In media appearances, Zacharia has repeatedly described herself as a lawyer. But the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that while Zacharia sat for the California bar exam after graduating from law school, she "didn't pass." A senior administration official confirmed to NBC News that Zacharia did not pass the California bar exam. Reuters also investigated her credentials and "could not find records showing Zacharia was registered as an attorney or member of the bar in any U.S. state or the District of Columbia." Asked by reporters Tuesday on the South Lawn where she passed the bar, Zacharia twice replied, "When I moved to China." In a phone interview with the New York Times on Wednesday , Zacharia said she misheard the question. "I assumed the question was, 'Where were you after law school?'" she told the paper.  "That's all I could hear over the sound of Marine One.  And, wanting to respect protocol, the distance behind the president, kept me from moving closer to hear the question." Zacharia pointed out that it was only her second day on the job. White House press secretary Katie Zacharia looks on as President Trump speaks to reporters on the South Lawn on Oct. 13. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson In a statement to the Washington Post , the White House said that "Katie moved to China with her husband after graduating because of his job at an American private equity firm while she worked on international transaction law." According to USA Today , Zacharia "worked for a Chinese law firm's international-practice team on multimillion-dollar shareholder agreements involving investments through the World Bank." She did not attempt to take the bar exam a second time. On Thursday, Zacharia confimed that she did not pass the bar, telling the conservative outlet Real America's Voice that she was "incredibly distracted and overwhelmed and excited" at the time by her impending marriage and move to China. "We just said… 'I'll take the bar and see what happens,'" Zacharia recalled. "The results are somewhat inconsequential because I knew I wouldn't need the bar in China." On Wednesday, a nonprofit watchdog group called Campaign for Accountability filed a complaint with the California bar asking it to investigate whether Zacharia had violated state law by "repeatedly holding herself out as a lawyer." White House spokesperson Steven Cheung responded on social media by dismissing the Campaign for Accountability as a "radical leftist-organization run by rabid numbskulls suffering from a severe case of Trump Derangement Syndrome." Legal experts told the Times that it's debatable whether a law school graduate can describe herself as a "lawyer" before she passes the bar. But she cannot call herself an "attorney" — someone who is licensed to practice law and give legal advice — nor can she serve as a "general counsel" or as an "associate" at a Chinese law firm, they added. Zacharia told Real America's Voice that she was "very careful about how I executed this and I never came across as somebody who was an attorney-at-law." "I consulted for a very long time many people in the field — 'Is it OK and acceptable if I label myself 'lawyer' … and provide legal analysis, not legal advice,"  she explained. "They said, 'Absolutely,' across the board. 'You can call yourself a lawyer.'" On Thursday night, Fox News host Sean Hannity pressed Zacharia on her halting explanation . "Why not just say, 'I went to Pepperdine Law School and then took a different career path, and I took the bar once and didn't pass it'?" Hannity asked. "Why get into this long drawn-out thing about the difference between a lawyer and an attorney?" "When I moved back to the United States, I didn't retake the bar," Zacharia said. "I had four kids in six years. It was never my intent to go into the practice of law." What happened in Zacharia's first briefing? White House press secretary Katie Zacharia speaks with reporters in the  Briefing Room on Oct. 13. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson Zacharia's first briefing lasted 15 minutes, most of which was taken up by her opening statement. "I am so honored to work for President Trump and the American people as the new White House press secretary," Zacharia told reporters in the Briefing Room. "I want to thank President Trump for his trust that he has placed in me. I have wanted to work with him for a very long time." She took questions from three news outlets — Breitbart, Fox News and the Daily Mail — before ending the briefing. Asked what she planned to do as press secretary, Zacharia said, "I get to do what I was doing on the outside already, which was getting to amplify, multiply and expand upon President Trump's incredible agenda for the American people." In his post on Truth Social announcing her appointment, Trump said Zacharia "has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning." Zacharia called the appointment "the honor of a lifetime" in a post on X . Who is Katie Zacharia? President Donald Trump and Katie Zacharia. Katie Zacharia/X The 42-year-old California native and mother of four left her role as senior communications adviser to Trump Media and Technology Group, which runs Truth Social, to join the White House. Before that, she served for about two months as a deputy assistant secretary and spokesperson for former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, according to her LinkedIn profile . She was best known for her frequent appearances defending the administration's policies on Fox News, CNN, Newsmax, One America News and other outlets. She told CNN in April — around the time she left DHS — that she's a "huge fan of ICE and a big fan of the Border Patrol." Zacharia first came to Washington in 2006 to intern for the Republican National Committee while George W. Bush was president. She lives in California with her husband and their four young children. During Tuesday's briefing, she was asked about juggling the competing roles of being a mother and White House press secretary. "The idea of not spending evenings with my kids is completely unacceptable," Zacharia said, before confusing her spouse with her boss. "So my president — excuse me, my husband — is out here." Zacharia then praised Trump as the "most family-friendly president we've ever had" and said her family will be moving from California to Washington, D.C., soon. CNN reported on Friday that Zacharia's "selection came about quickly" and that she "was not being considered for the role" as of "last week." CNN also reported that "on multiple occasions, senior officials had narrowed down the list" of possible press secretaries "only to find that candidates had said something negative about the president, disqualifying them from the position." In a New York Post column in February , Zacharia recounted a clash with liberal patrons of her "local cardio kickboxing gym" that ended with the gym owner asking her not to wear her red "Team Trump 2024" hat to exercise class. "I responded that I would never take my Trump hat off to appease the left," Zacharia wrote. "I refuse to stay silent." articles.title: Trump officials scrutinized Omar in 2019. They didn't find citizenship issues.
articles.summary: Seven years ago, a political appointee in the first Trump administration approached U.S. immigration authorities with a request that alarmed career staffers: Scrub the immigration records of Rep. Ilhan Omar, then a newly elected Democratic lawmaker from Minnesota, for evidence of fraud. That 2019 demand, detailed by three former immigration officials, struck staffers at the time as a highly unusual effort to wield federal power to dig up compromising material on a sitting member of Congress who was a prominent critic of President Donald Trump. Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. The request sparked a swift review examining Omar’s history, her family’s past as Somali refugees resettled in the United States and rumors that had circulated for years in conservative media over her marriage. Homeland Security Investigations - the investigative arm of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement - ultimately determined there was insufficient evidence of wrongdoing, one of the former officials said. The idea of pursuing a full investigation was eventually abandoned. Now, though, with Trump back in the White House and his administration using federal power to take aim at perceived enemies, Omar has once again found herself in federal crosshairs. She is now facing an inquiry over some of the same allegations investigators previously deemed not worth pursuing. The current effort - which burst into public view Monday as federal agents descended upon Omar’s D.C. home - is focused on whether she or her father lied on paperwork they submitted to obtain legal status and eventual citizenship after arriving in the U.S. in the 1990s. Investigators are reexamining questions about Omar’s birth date and her late father’s past military history in Somalia, which had passed scrutiny during the 2019 review. Depending on their findings, the administration could seek to charge Omar with a crime or move to challenge her status in the country. But such a step would be a sharp reversal of the earlier review, which found no issue with her naturalization, one of the former officials familiar with the earlier effort said. “I think her citizenship is solid and there wasn’t any fraud there,” the ex-official said. Omar has dismissed the revived investigation as yet another example of the Justice Department, under Trump, attempting “to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.” “Trump has spread lie after lie about the Congresswoman in a desperate attempt to justify his extraordinary abuse of power,” her spokesperson said in a statement Thursday. “This is politically motivated and an escalation of Trump’s personal vendetta against her lasting over a decade.” This account of the Trump administration’s current and past efforts to investigate and possibly build a case against Omar is based on interviews with a dozen people, many of whom spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss nonpublic details of those probes. Several current and former officials raised questions about the scope, tactics and motivations driving the current Omar investigation, which they say appears to be disregarding key norms on how immigration reviews are typically handled and bypassing guardrails intended to ensure federal inquiries, including those looking into sitting lawmakers, are not perceived to be driven by politics. A spokesperson for the Justice Department said the agency does not comment on ongoing investigations. The Department of Homeland Security referred questions to the Justice Department. Questions about the probe came into play ahead of this week’s highly public search of Omar’s home. Before carrying out the search, prosecutors spent days working to allay concerns from a federal judge that their plans could run afoul of constitutional protections shielding members of Congress from unwarranted executive branch intrusion, according to three people familiar with the matter. U.S. Magistrate Judge Matthew J. Sharbaugh, who ultimately signed off on the warrant, first imposed strict conditions on how the search should be carried out, the people said. His limits on the search appeared intended to ensure that the warrant fell in line with the D.C. court’s interpretation of the Constitution’s speech and debate clause, which generally shields lawmakers’ legislative duties and actions from criminal probes. As part of the search, agents removed boxes of documents and seized Omar’s cellphone and passport, one person familiar with the matter said. Trump has assailed Omar for years, and this week condemned her again on social media and public remarks. “I think she’s a terrible person,” he told reporters. “But that’s really up to the DOJ. I have nothing to do with it.” Trump’s administration has also made clear its scrutiny on Omar is not limited to immigration issues. Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney in D.C., announced Tuesday her office had launched its own investigation into Omar’s personal finances, tied to disclosure statements she filed in Congress last year and separate from the immigration probe. Pirro, a former Fox News host, once drew a highly unusual public rebuke from the network in 2019 for on-air comments suggesting that Omar, as a Muslim, could not be loyal to the U.S. Constitution. Omar’s office has previously dismissed questions raised by House Republicans over her financial disclosure statements as a right-wing attempt to “manufacture controversy.” However, federal prosecutors’ interest in the finances of Omar extend back to the Biden administration, according to two people familiar with the effort. Those individuals said it was not clear why the investigation during the prior administration appeared to have stalled. But the revived immigration investigation into Omar appears to be the furthest along and the administration’s higher priority. Alessandra P. Serano, an associate deputy attorney general who is playing a key role in the probe, went before the judge seeking the search warrant for Omar’s home, two people familiar with the matter said. Attorney General Todd Blanche also recently dispatched Serano, a trusted aide, to Florida to check in on the high-profile and struggling Florida-based investigation into former Obama and Biden-era officials, according to multiple people. Authorities have issued more than a dozen subpoenas related to Omar and the investigation into her, including some to her siblings, seeking testimony before a grand jury in Minneapolis in the coming weeks, two people said. The Washington Post has reported that investigators are focused on whether Omar or her father, Nur Omar Mohamed, intentionally misstated her birth date on immigration paperwork so she could be eligible to derive citizenship through him as a minor when he was naturalized in 2000. Investigators are also scrutinizing whether Omar’s father may have purposefully lied or omitted information on his past military service in Somalia that could have made him ineligible to obtain legal status in the country. But three former officials involved in the 2019 review of Omar’s immigration file said both of those issues were considered during that inquiry. An official with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, who was normally tasked with scrutinizing the backgrounds of people including serious criminals, terrorists and potential national security threats, was asked in 2019 to review Omar’s background. The then-freshman lawmaker had emerged as a frequent focus of conservative attacks. At the time, the agency was primarily focused on possible fraud related to Omar’s marriage to her former husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi. Right-wing commentators had repeatedly pressed unsubstantiated claims that Omar and Elmi were siblings who carried out a sham marriage so that Elmi could obtain U.S. immigration benefits. Elmi had previously filed an immigration petition related to his marriage-based green card that would move it from conditional status to permanent. USCIS requested additional evidence due to concerns over the validity of his marriage, but Elmi withdrew the application following that request, one of the former officials said. Elmi could not immediately be reached for comment Thursday. The 2019 review of Omar also looked at other issues, some of which are being examined anew. For instance, back then, USCIS quickly determined it could not accurately answer questions over Omar’s age because refugees frequently come from countries with little or no birth records, making it hard to determine with any certainty. “That’s not strange and that’s not a red flag to me,” one of the former officials said. “It’s just very, very common that there aren’t great birth records.” The agency also examined Omar’s father’s immigration file but did not find any issues, according to the former official. The USCIS officer tasked with vetting Omar produced a memo of those findings and shared it with a senior USCIS official and a fraud detention official before the effort was ultimately abandoned, the person said. Due to the sensitivity, the memo was printed out, and distributed in person, and not shared over email. Whether the current investigation will uncover more substantial evidence to back the administration’s fraud claims remains to be seen. Even if the Trump administration finds wrongdoing, any attempt to strip her citizenship would likely be lengthy and result in a legal battle. The administration, however, is also exploring the possibility that it could seek to revoke her citizenship certificate if the current investigation does not result in criminal charges or a conviction, a senior Trump administration official said. Revocation is a rarely employed USCIS administrative process that can be used to cancel the document due to fraud or an error. The process is not restricted to a certain period of time like criminal denaturalizations, which are subject to a 10-year statute of limitations. The revocation would not remove her citizenship but would make it challenging to obtain some government documents. This action could open the door to immigration-related charges and possibly removal proceedings, though such a novel application of the administrative authority would almost certainly face challenges from Omar in court. In a statement, Omar’s spokesperson assailed the Trump administration’s efforts to target the congresswoman. “He has lied about her family, about her immigration history, and about her love of this country,” the statement read. “But the truth is that Trump’s push to strip her of her citizenship and deport her has no basis in the law and has no precedent. This isn’t a legitimate law enforcement action.” Alexei Koseff contributed to this report. articles.title: Kristi Noem no longer serving as Trump envoy to Shield of the Americas
articles.summary: Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem is no longer serving as the Trump administration's special envoy for the Shield of the Americas initiative, a State Department official said Thursday, though she remains involved in the administration's efforts to coordinate security cooperation across the Western Hemisphere. "Kristi Noem's envoy status expired last month and she is no longer in the role," a State Department official told CBS News Thursday. "She is now a senior advisor to Deputy Secretary Landau and continues to work on the Shield of the Americas portfolio." The Shield of the Americas is a coalition made up of the United States and several Caribbean and Latin American countries established by the Trump administration earlier this year to cooperate on economic matters, anti-cartel enforcement and other issues. In a statement on X, Noem said her role as special envoy "was always a six-month appointment." Noem's envoy designation expired just before the United Nations General Assembly last month in New York, where she continued participating in diplomatic meetings connected to the initiative. On Sept. 22, she met with Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa, whose government publicly identified her as the special envoy for the Shield of the Americas. She also attended a gathering of Shield of the Americas leaders hosted by President Trump, where he publicly acknowledged her work. "I want to thank Kristi Noem for doing a really terrific job," Mr. Trump said during his remarks. Noem was appointed special envoy for the Shield of the Americas in March, after she was removed as homeland security secretary amid mounting scrutiny of her management of the department and the influence of her adviser, Corey Lewandowski. Her transition to the envoy role coincided with a five-country tour of Latin America and the Caribbean in March, much of which took place as she completed her tenure as homeland security secretary. Lewandowski appeared in photographs during those visits, though the State Department later clarified he had no formal position at the department. Her public activities in the envoy role appear to have been limited, and included meeting Noboa in Quito on March 25, holding discussions with Ecuadorian and Colombian diplomats in Washington in September, and participating in meetings with regional leaders on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly. This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/kristi-noem-no-longer-trump-envoy-shield-of-the-americas/

articles.title: ICE officer who struck man with vehicle put on leave as DA weighs charges
articles.summary: The Immigrations Customs and Enforcement officer who allegedly struck a man with a vehicle during a pursuit outside Houston last weekend has been placed on administrative leave, the agency said. The move is standard for all use-of-force incidents, according to an ICE spokesperson. "This incident is under active internal investigation," the spokesperson said in a statement Friday. On Saturday, Miguel Parra-Hernandez was hit by a car operated by an ICE agent during an arrest as the unidentified officer attempted to arrest him and another suspect, the agency said. Parra-Hernandez, who ICE alleged is undocumented, is currently in the hospital recovering from injuries to his legs, according to the Harris County District Attorney's office. Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare said Parra-Hernandez broke his leg in three places and has undergone two surgeries. KTRK - PHOTO: Law enforcement officials are at the scene after a man was struck by a vehicle driven by an ICE agent during chase, according to the Harris Courty Sheriff's Office, on Oct. 10, 2026, in Harris County, Texas. Parra-Hernandez has not been charged by any law enforcement agency as of Thursday, according to the DA's office. ICE agent strikes man with car during pursuit in Texas, authorities say ICE said in a statement that that one of its officers was pursuing Jose Mendoza-Cervantes, a Mexican national who they allege had a criminal record and a final order of removal by a judge, and observed him get in a vehicle with Parra-Hernandez Saturday morning. The ICE officer attempted a car stop, and Mendoza-Cervantes and Parra-Hernandez fled their vehicle on foot, according to ICE and the Harris County Sheriff's Office. Surveillance video of the incident reviewed by ABC News appears to show the ICE vehicle moving in the direction of a man running and then striking him. - PHOTO: In this screengrab from a video, a man is shown running prior to being struck by a vehicle driven by an ICE agent, according to the Harris Courty Sheriff's Office, on Oct. 10, 2026, in Harris County, Texas. An ICE spokesperson alleged in a statement that Parra-Hernandez "ran in front of an ICE vehicle" when he was hit. "Allegations that ICE struck Miguel Parra-Hernandez intentionally are RECKLESS and FALSE. The men and women of ICE are entrusted with upholding the rule of law and are held to the highest standards of professionalism, integrity, and ethical conduct," the spokesperson said in a statement Wednesday. Mendoza-Cervantes remains at large as of Friday, according to ICE. DA looking to interview 2 witnesses in backseat of ICE vehicle in Houston incident Teare, the DA, is currently probing the situation and told ABC News Wednesday that his office could possibly pursue criminal charges against the ICE officer. The DA's office said two people were allegedly detained by the ICE agent prior to the incident and in the back seat of the ICE officer's vehicle when Parra-Hernandez was hit. Teare told ABC News Thursday that his office was able to interview one of those witnesses before they were deported and that he believes the ICE officer intentionally struck Parra-Hernandez. "Thankfully, we were able to meet with him in custody yesterday, but we were the only individuals to even speak to him," the DA told ABC News. articles.title: A powerful El Niño could disrupt winter getaways. Here's what travelers should know.
articles.summary: As travelers look to escape the cold for warm weather over the holiday season, an unusually strong El Niño could lead to unseasonal weather in several popular vacation destinations. The climate pattern, which occurs when waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become unusually warm, can shift weather patterns across the country, potentially affecting popular winter getaways from Florida to the Caribbean. "El Niños are associated with more storminess across the southern tier of the country, and potentially more ice storms across the southern plains," Matthew Rosencrans, a meteorologist at NOAA's Weather Prediction Center, told Yahoo. Those conditions can significantly disrupt travel, the meteorologist said, but the effects will be far from uniform. El Niño winters are also often warmer, Rosencrans explained, which can sometimes benefit travel across the northern tier of the contiguous U.S. Meanwhile, parts of the Caribbean may see drier weather, creating very different conditions for travelers depending on their destination. Where winter travelers could feel the effects Travelers heading to Florida this winter for a holiday getaway could face wetter-than-usual conditions, with El Niño increasing the likelihood of rainfall and severe weather across parts of the Southeast. "For Florida, it often means a fairly robust secondary severe weather season in November and into December across the Southeast and Florida," Rosencrans told Yahoo. NOAA's Climate Prediction Center outlook , released Oct. 15, gives the Southeast and Florida the greatest likelihood of a wetter-than-normal winter, with odds above 70% in some parts of northern Florida through the January to March period. Temperatures are forecast to be near normal across much of the Southeast. The winter seasonal precipitation outlook, according to NOAA. NOAA That doesn't necessarily mean travelers need to rethink a Florida vacation, but those hoping for uninterrupted beach weather should keep an eye on the forecast. While Florida could see a wetter winter, the Caribbean islands may see less rain, though it varies by island and time of year. "The Caribbean can often see drier weather during El Niño events, more strongly in the summer months from reduced tropical activity," Rosencrans explained. The ABC islands, Aruba, Bonaire and Curaçao, are one example of where less rain is likely. Their main rainy season typically runs from October through January, with the dry season arriving later, from February through May. An El Niño suppresses that rainy season, according to the Meteorological Department of Curaçao . While lower rainfall over the islands may sound appealing, Rosencrans said it can mean fewer thunderstorms and make days feel hotter "as there is less cloudiness and continuous sunshine." Other islands show no clear lean either way. NOAA's winter outlook , released Oct. 15, gives Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands "equal chances of below-average, near-average or above-average seasonal total precipitation amounts" for December through February. Could El Niño affect hurricane season? El Niño has helped suppress Atlantic hurricane activity this year, but that doesn't mean the threat of tropical storms has disappeared. This year, Isaias became the first Atlantic hurricane of the season late on Oct. 7, making it one day shy of tying a 121-year-old record for the basin's latest-forming hurricane, according to the Associated Press . Lindsey Long, a meteorologist at NOAA's Weather Prediction Center, told Yahoo that wind shear linked to El Niño is still inhibiting storm development across the Atlantic. "In a typical year, we would expect about two additional hurricanes to develop between mid-October and November 30," Long said. By mid-October, the Atlantic would typically have had at least five, according to the National Hurricane Center , as reported by NPR . This year, Isaias is the first. However, the Gulf has been less affected by that wind shear and has extremely warm surface waters that could fuel storms, Long said. Formation typically shifts from the Atlantic's main development region, which stretches from the Caribbean to the African coast, toward the Gulf at this time of year. "There is still a continued possibility for tropical development throughout the remainder of the season," Long told Yahoo. The expert did add that a possible shift in when hurricane season starts or ends would not be connected to El Niño. Travelers heading to hurricane-prone areas may want to consider flexible booking options and review their travel insurance policies to understand what weather-related disruptions are covered. articles.title: Fed chair warns AI spending could fuel inflation and pledges to contain prices
articles.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh warned of a potential "shock" to the U.S. economy delivered by a rise in artificial intelligence spending , pledging to contain price increases as a flood of private sector funds drives up demand. "If you’re a central banker, you’re in the business of trying to ensure stable prices and full employment, you’ve got to recognize this as a shock," Warsh said in Bangkok, Thailand, at a conference organized by the International Monetary Fund. A surge in AI spending has helped boost the U.S. economy in recent quarters. In theory, an onrush of investment in activities like chip manufacturing and data center construction could put upward pressure in general on consumer prices, unless the demand is offset by a new supply of goods and services. Which grocery prices are rising the fastest and which are falling? "It’s obviously hitting the demand side of the economy before it’s hitting the supply side of the economy," Warsh said. Warsh, who took the helm of the Fed in May, has previously weighed in on the potential impact of AI on the labor market and wider economy. On Friday, Warsh reiterated his optimism about AI, saying the technology would ultimately generate added productivity and wealth. But, Warsh added, "the path from where we are to there is likely to be a very bumpy one." "We really don’t know what the market structure will be of these new technologies," Warsh said. "Who's going to be making the money?" Warsh acknowledged other shocks faced by the U.S. economy, including "shocks of war and military conflict." Eli Hartman/Bloomberg via Getty Images - PHOTO: The Nscale data center project in Barstow, Texas, Oct. 15, 2026. The outbreak of the Iran war in February imposed a historic oil supply shock and caused an acceleration of price increases in many countries. A U.S. government report issued this week showed inflation had climbed to a 4-month high in September as the Middle East conflict continued to drive up gasoline prices. Prices rose 3.7% in September, according to new data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics . Inflation stands more than a percentage point higher than the Fed's target rate of 2%. "It’s hard to be in a discussion with central bankers and not compare notes and hear the same thing about the surge in prices," Warsh said on Friday. He later added: "I’ve heard resolve from my colleagues around the world to deliver price stability. I’ve certainly delivered that resolve." Price hikes prompted the Fed to raise interest rates a quarter of a percentage point in September, marking the central bank's first rate increase since 2023. An increase to the benchmark interest rate aims to slash inflation by slowing the economy and eating away at demand, though the policy typically yields results after a lag time lasting several months. The next meeting of Fed policymakers takes place on Oct. 28, just days before the midterm elections. Gas prices set record for highest number of days above $4 a gallon in a calendar year Consistent with his approach in previous public appearances, Warsh opted against issuing a forecast about what the central bank may do at its meeting later this month. "I don’t pre-judge meetings. I don’t believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings we have over the balance of this year," Warsh said. Many investors appeared to interpret Warsh's posture as a sign the Fed may hold interest rates steady later this month. As of Friday morning, investors peg the chance of the Fed maintaining current interest rates at about 86%, which marks an uptick from about 55% on Wednesday, according to CME Group’s FedWatch Tool , a measure of market sentiment. articles.title: 'You should be ashamed of yourself': Heated Senate debates become personal
articles.summary: WCSH Candidates faced off in heated debates Thursday night in two of the country’s most competitive Senate races , showing how bitter — and personal — each contest has become. In Maine, Democratic nominee Troy Jackson told GOP Sen. Susan Collins to “shut up” after she suggested a protester was one of his supporters. And in Alaska, Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan questioned Democratic opponent Mary Peltola’s “character” while citing allegations she mistreated staff. “I think that Alaskans have had it up to here with the lying and dishonesty,” Peltola said during another exchange. “Dan, you should be ashamed of yourself.” The races are unfolding thousands of miles apart but both critical to the Senate majority. Collins, a moderate Republican, is seeking reelection in a blue state, while Sullivan is running for another term in more GOP-leaning Alaska where Peltola, a former congresswoman, is well-known. Both debates showed how much of a political liability President Donald Trump’s war in Iran has become for Republican incumbents. Sullivan said it “needs to end soon,” while Collins continued to insist Trump should have consulted Congress on the conflict. Here’s a look at key moments from the debates. US Sen. Susan Collins and Democratic candidate for the US Senate Troy Jackson are seen during their debate at the Gracie Theatre in Bangor, Maine on Thursday. - Charly Triballeau/AFP/Getty Images A protester disrupts Collins on data centers The fourth and final Senate debate in Maine grew heated as Collins and Jackson sharpened their attacks. Within minutes, a protester shouted at Collins about the impact of data centers, forcing the debate to a brief halt. “AI data centers are destroying our climate. They are poisoning our waters,” the protester yelled. Following the incident, Collins said the protester “is obviously one of Troy’s supporters.” “Oh, shut up,” Jackson replied, saying he did not know who the person was. unknown content item - Corruption allegations and campaign financing in Maine During the Collins-Jackson debate, both candidates tried to portray their opponent as corrupt, a major theme that has loomed over the hotly contested race and the midterms nationally. Collins cornered Jackson for not sharing his FEC report with her on Wednesday, a promise he made at their debate earlier this week. Jackson said he missed his self-imposed deadline because it took longer to process the donations from 200,000 people to his campaign than he expected. “I had to make sure this report was right. It was my first one,” Jackson said. Throughout the campaign, Jackson has framed Collins as being influenced by her donors and touted that he doesn’t take any corporate PAC money. Collins tried to flip the script on Thursday by dinging Jackson for running joint ads with his party’s Senate campaign arm, which does take money from corporations, and for not disclosing his donors. Jackson said he did not control their donations to the Senate campaign committee but did concede his campaign has taken money from billionaires. “That is accurate. But I haven’t made any deals like Senator Collins has with those billionaires. I don’t owe them any votes. I am going to tax those billionaires when I get to the US Senate. So, if they want to give me money during this campaign, I guess that’s up to them,” Jackson said. When it was Jackson’s turn to ask Collins a question, he got personal. In defending his credentials and pushing back on Collins’ critique that he doesn’t have the right experience, Jackson exclaimed, “Is it just me that you look down on or is it working-class people overall?” Collins further distances from Trump on Iran war Collins doubled down on her criticism of the Iran war as the Maine Republican continues to distance herself from Trump. When asked if Congress should have been consulted before Trump decided to go to war, Collins said, “Congress definitely should have been consulted.” But Collins added that that the War Powers Resolution gave Trump the flexibility to act unilaterally within the first 60 days of the conflict, which she said is why she did not start voting to rein in Trump’s war powers until after those initial 60 days had passed. unknown content item - Iran war’s consequences also hangs over Alaska debate Sullivan repeatedly had to grapple with issues where Trump has not made the race easy for him. The war in Iran, for example, has led to especially high fuel costs in Alaska. Sullivan said he has opposed limiting Trump’s Iran powers because he supports the overall goal of preventing the country from obtaining a nuclear weapon. But he said the war “needs to end soon.” “The energy costs from this war are too high, but … the best way to bring down costs with regard to energy in Alaska is to produce more energy by and for Alaskans,” Sullivan said, suggesting Peltola could not be trusted to support that. Peltola blamed Washington politicians for “waging forever wars that are skyrocketing our costs.” And she scoffed at Sullivan’s pivot to the topic of domestic energy production. “I have been a strong supporter of drilling in Alaska,” she said. “That is not the issue here.” Sullivan continued to show daylight with Trump when asked about Trump’s plan to buy Russian diesel . He reiterated his opposition, saying, “I don’t think it’s a good ideal at all,” and noting he “just led the effort” to pass new sanctions on Russia in Congress. Sullivan, Peltola spar over her treatment of staff Sullivan and Peltola clashed twice over a September story from The New York Times that alleged staff mistreatment by Peltola. In the article, her campaign pushed back on the suggestion she regularly abused her staff but said she occasionally “struggled to deal with her grief” after her mother and husband died in 2023. “I do not think that this election is about me on my worst day, and I found so many of these allegations concerning and outright fabrications or mass exaggerations of the truth,” Peltola said at the debate when asked about the Times report. Sullivan emphasized that the story was based on interviews with nine former staff members and at least 20 other people. “It’s not Mary Peltola on her worst day,” Sullivan said. “It’s Mary Peltola over the course of a couple years with dozens of people weighing in on this.” Sullivan brought up the Times story on his own earlier in the debate, saying Peltola has “treated young Alaskans horribly” and that it was “a character flaw.” Peltola called it “gossip” and “unfounded allegations” as Sullivan talked over her. “It’s the New York Times,” he said. “Read the article.” Sullivan questions whether Peltola got questions in advance The Times story was not the only cause for animosity between the two candidates. After Peltola criticized Sullivan about the war in Iran, looking down at notes on her podium as she spoke, Sullivan turned to the moderators. “We weren’t supposed to get these questions beforehand were, we?” he asked. “No, sir,” one moderator said before another added: “Neither one of you got questions beforehand. Absolutely not.” “OK,” Sullivan said. “I’m just watching my opponent read from questions that seem to be answered.” “I’m prepared,” Peltola said. Sullivan appeared to back down from his suggestion while speaking with reporters after the debate, according to Alaska Public Media , which quoted him telling the hosts, “I’m not blaming you guys.” This story has been updated with additional information. articles.summary: 苹果首款折叠屏iPhone预购爆单，分析师上调销售预期，股价小幅走高。 苹果公司周五表示，旗下首款折叠屏手机iPhone Duo的预购需求"非同寻常"。 预购通道开放后数分钟内，发货估期即从11月滑至12月，最终延至明年1月底，所有颜色及存储配置均受影响。 彭博智库分析师在周五发布的报告中指出， iPhone Duo的销量可能超越此前预估的1400万部及280亿美元，若苹果能够成功吸引现有Pro和Pro Max用户转换至该折叠机型，iPhone平均售价将分别提升82%和67%。 苹果股价周五上涨0.43%，报343.46美元。 预购需求远超预期，发货期延至明年 iPhone Duo于周五上午开放预购后，大量消费者随即在苹果在线商店遭遇发货延迟。 起初，发货估期推至11月，随后在数分钟内迅速滑落至12月，最终延伸至明年1月底。延迟覆盖该设备的全部颜色选项及从256GB至2TB的所有存储配置。苹果在声明中表示： iPhone Duo，我们的首款折叠屏iPhone的预购需求非同寻常。我们正全力以赴，尽快将这款革命性新品送达消费者手中，并将持续接受在线订单。 苹果同时表示，其团队期待消费者莅临全球各地的苹果零售店亲身体验iPhone Duo及完整iPhone产品线，但未披露10月23日正式开售当天实体门店是否备有现货供未能抢到预购的消费者购买。 据市场调研机构Counterpoint Research本周发布的报告，iPhone 18 Pro系列新机的开售表现"强于前代"，在中国和印度市场尤为突出。 iPhone Duo所针对的，正是此前分析人士描述的"愿意为旗舰体验支付溢价的高端小众群体"。但从预购首日的市场反应来看，这一群体的规模或远大于初始预期。苹果表示，iPhone Duo的首批交付将于10月23日启动，官网同时提示消费者于10月24日起查询店内自取库存。 定价创历史新高，供应受限早有预兆 iPhone Duo起售价为1,999美元，最高配置（2TB存储）售价达3,200美元，创苹果iPhone定价历史纪录。该机型搭载7.6英寸内屏及精工设计的铰链，并针对折叠形态重新设计了iOS体验。 供应受限并非完全出乎意料。据彭博此前报道，iPhone Duo在发布前已有传言指制造难度较高，可能导致供货紧张。 苹果还面临今年消费电子行业普遍存在的元器件短缺问题，尤其是内存芯片供应不足，这也迫使其在全线产品上提高售价。 以历史先例来看，此次延误规模尤为罕见。苹果素以高效的全球供应链管理著称，延误极为少见。据英国《金融时报》报道，上一次出现类似情况是2022年新冠疫情期间，工厂停产导致iPhone 14部分订单延误逾一个月。 分析师上调预期，折叠机型或推高均价 据彭博，彭博智库分析师Anurag Rana和Josh Christensen在周五的研报中指出，iPhone Duo销量有望超越此前针对苹果2027财年设定的1400万部及280亿美元销售额预估。 两位分析师进一步指出，若苹果能够成功说服现有iPhone Pro及Pro Max用户转向该折叠入门机型，将推动iPhone整体平均售价分别提升82%和67%。iPhone Duo售价为1999美元。 iPhone Duo是苹果新任首席执行官John Ternus上任以来最具分量的产品发布之一。iPhone Duo搭载7.6英寸内屏及经过精心设计的铰链结构，并配备针对折叠形态优化的iOS新体验。 John Ternus于今年9月接任CEO一职，上任以来已相继推出HomeView智能家居中枢等新品。 据彭博报道，苹果还将于本月晚些时候推出搭载触控屏幕的MacBook Pro及其他设备。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 信贷恐慌击穿AI交易：CoreWeave债券收益率维持高位，纳指创6月底来最大单周跌幅
articles.summary: 美国股市周五全线下跌，投资者对人工智能相关企业能否及时产生足够利润以偿付高企债务的忧虑持续发酵，科技板块首当其冲。纳斯达克综合指数本周累计下挫约4.5%，创下自6月26日当周以来最大单周跌幅。 市场对AI基础设施企业债务风险的担忧持续升温，CoreWeave部分债券收益率周四一度突破15%，周五仍然维持高位。CoreWeave股价周五再度重挫12%，较年内高点已累计下跌逾50%。 与此同时，美联储主席沃什在曼谷国际货币基金组织活动上拒绝就10月利率会议前景提供任何指引，令市场缺乏政策方向支撑，长端美债收益率随油价上涨及通胀顾虑进一步走高，10年期国债收益率升至5.097%。 半导体及科技股的抛售浪潮自周三起蔓延至亚洲市场，韩国综合股价指数本周重挫14%，为2008年全球金融危机以来最大单周跌幅，距夏季峰值已下跌逾37%。 信贷压力成为科技股核心痛点 科技板块下跌的深层逻辑，在于市场对AI商业化节奏与融资成本之间错配的担忧日益加剧。 CoreWeave至少借款350亿美元用于建设数据中心，尽管获得了其最大供应商之一、英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的公开背书，但股价仍单日下跌12%。 对冲基金公司Sibilla Capital创始人兼首席投资官Lorenzo Di Mattia表示， "随着信贷和资本成本上升至难以承受的水平，各公司迟早将不得不缩减计划、削减资本支出。"Lorenzo Di Mattia称，他目前持有少量美国股市空头头寸。 英伟达股价下跌1.4%至214.13美元，另一家CoreWeave供应商戴尔科技则下挫4.6%至451.71美元，戴尔本周累计跌超22%，为其2018年重新上市以来最大单周跌幅。 CBOE Global Markets高级副总裁JJ Kinahan指出，"我们正处于高风险区域，但这类信贷压力往往会催生并购活动，这是此类情况下的常见结果。" 美联储态度审慎，债市长短端分化 美债市场呈现明显的期限分化走势，反映出市场对通胀与增长前景的复杂预判。 10年期美债收益率上涨0.011个百分点至5.097%，30年期国债收益率上涨0.009个百分点至5.436%，部分弥补了周四的跌幅，但仍录得逾一年来最大单周降幅。 相比之下，2年期国债收益率下行0.013个百分点至4.734%，完成了自8月以来最大单周回落。 沃什在曼谷国际货币基金组织活动上的表态整体偏谨慎，拒绝就10月议息会议的利率走向提供前瞻指引。油价上涨及更广泛的通胀顾虑，构成长端收益率上行的主要驱动力。 市场结构性分化：银行与防御性科技相对抗跌 在普跌格局下，部分板块展现出相对韧性，显示市场内部存在明显分化。 金融板块成为为数不多的亮点之一，M&T Bank和Citizens Financial等地区性银行控股公司的季报业绩普遍强劲。苹果股价微涨0.4%至343.46美元，该公司在AI布局上一贯较同行审慎，其可折叠智能手机iPhone Duo的初期订单情况良好。 网络安全领域，Varonis Systems股价上涨2.9%至48.72美元，此前非上市公司Proofpoint宣布以约63亿美元收购这家数据安全公司，以强化其在AI安全领域的布局。 小盘股方面，罗素2000指数进一步滑入回调区间，年内涨幅收窄至约10%。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

，预计归母净利润1310亿元至1325亿元，较上年同期亏损52.80亿元大幅扭亏；营业收入预计2650亿元至2700亿元，同比增长逾七倍。公司将业绩改善归因于AI算力需求带动全球DRAM景气度提升、产品供不应求价格大幅上涨。董事长朱一明提议回购10亿至20亿元股份。 长安汽车管理层大变阵 ，朱华荣继续担任中国长安汽车集团党委书记、董事长，不再兼任上市公司重庆长安汽车董事长，集团总经理赵非接任上市公司董事长，原常务执行副总裁叶沛出任总裁。此次调整距离朱华荣获选连任上市公司董事长不足一个月。今年前三季度上市公司长安汽车累计销量169.27万辆，同比下降18.07%。 北汽蓝谷拟为北汽新能源增资不超过21.38亿元 ，其中上市公司出资不超过10亿元、北汽集团出资不超过6.38亿元，另通过公开挂牌引入不超过5亿元外部投资，主要用于补充日常经营流动资金。今年前三季度北汽新能源累计销量16.34万辆、同比增长46.52%，上半年营收115.97亿元、归母净亏损19.38亿元。 理想汽车芯片子公司完成首轮融资 ，上海马赫心科技签署首轮股权融资协议，认购总额16.25亿元，理想汽车出资10亿元、外部投资方合计6.25亿元，若追加认购权悉数行使，投后估值最高达171亿元。融资将用于芯片及域控制器研发与商业化，推进面向外部客户的产品供应。马赫M100采用5nm车规级工艺、单颗算力1280 TOPS，已搭载于新一代理想量产车型。 海外 美芯片股八连跌，市值蒸发约2万亿美元 ，费城半导体指数连续第八个交易日下跌，创2008年金融危机以来最长连跌纪录，本周累跌11.4%，八个交易日累计跌逾13%。若按各股较52周高点跌幅计算，整个板块损失市值约达4万亿美元，但该指数年内仍累涨约60%。美光本周跌14.6%，存储芯片指数累跌17.6%；CoreWeave周五再跌11.9%，本周累计跌超25%。 - 费城半导体连跌八个交易日，黄仁勋："这一切终将过去" ：英伟达CEO在柏林表示市场动荡终将过去，AI变革才刚刚开始。 - 巴克莱：AI交易"最佳阶段"已过，芯片股暴跌是仓位出清而非基本面崩塌 ：高盛预测五大超大规模公司明年资本支出约1.2万亿美元。 沃什曼谷发言偏鸽，市场押注10月按兵不动 ，美联储主席沃什在IMF年会对话中重申致力于价格稳定，但明确表示"我不会预判会议结果"，市场对10月27日至28日会议加息的概率预期从约27%骤降至15%以下。高盛首席经济学家Jan Hatzius团队指出，结合其他官员表态，沃什此番讲话进一步表明美联储将在10月按兵不动，下次加息预计在12月落地。 - 美联储主席沃什：AI是我一生中最深远的经济变革，10月和12月议息会议至关重要 ：沃什称9月加息以来全球经济走势大体符合预期，并宣布放弃"前瞻指引"策略。 美国众议院两党议员提出议案阻击俄罗斯柴油协议 ，众议院外交事务委员会民主党首席委员Gregory Meeks提出的《禁止腐败的俄罗斯石油交易法》拟撤销财政部海外资产控制办公室已发放的第135号等一般许可，禁止未来继续发放豁免，并要求总统在法案生效30天内对参与俄罗斯油气开采、炼制及海上运输的主体实施制裁。议案消息公布后，美股午盘之初WTI原油一度接近100.90美元，布伦特原油一度逼近109.60美元。 美国拟提供最多1700万桶战略储备原油 ，能源部16日提出新一轮原油交换计划，交付时间为11月至次年1月，投标方须在2028年至2029年间归还原油并额外交付至少12.5%的溢价。该计划属于今年3月承诺提供1.72亿桶原油的一部分。美国战略石油储备规模目前为1.862亿桶，为1982年10月以来最低水平。今年6月类似交换因溢价过高，最终仅约50万桶获企业借用。 - IEA加速释放1亿桶原油储备，并承诺优先释放"2000万桶柴油" ：成员国已释放3.3亿桶，剩余1亿桶系补足3月承诺缺口，美欧在是否追加释放上存在分歧。 美财政部一级交易商调查未释放削减发债信号， 美债收益率走高、10年期重上5.12%。在征询一级交易商意见的调查中，美国财政部问到长期国债的回购计划、如何提高回购效率、短债发行时点、经济与融资前景，却没把问题直接指向减少长债供给。部分投资者原本期待，财政部会借此次问卷更明确地暗示正考虑缩减长债标售规模，甚至停止发行20年期国债。11月4日财政部公布的再融资公告成为下一观察点。花旗预计，届时会将20年和30年期美债标售规模各削减30亿美元，认为本次调查显示财政部在考虑减发长债。 美国2026财年赤字扩大至1.99万亿美元 ，较上一财年增长约12%，支出增长约6%至7.4万亿美元，收入增长约3%至5.4万亿美元。净利息支出增加814亿美元至1.05万亿美元，首次突破万亿美元门槛；全年总利息支出达1.360万亿美元，预计将于2028年底前超过社会保障支出。财政部将关税退款列为赤字扩大因素之一，2025年减税法案则令企业所得税收入下降逾700亿美元。 8月海外资金重返美债市场 ，美国财政部国际资本流动报告显示，8月海外投资者净买入美国国债1089亿美元，总持仓升至9.3317万亿美元。英国持仓史上首次突破万亿美元至1.0095万亿美元，加拿大增持383亿美元居首。日本持仓减少356亿美元至1.0683万亿美元、连续四个月下降；中国大陆持仓减少273亿美元至5907亿美元，连续两个月创2008年8月以来新低。 软银考虑收购美国最大安保公司 ，据彭博社报道，软银集团正就收购Allied Universal展开初步研究，可能给后者带来最高180亿美元的股权估值，叠加约120亿美元公开交易债务，交易总价值或接近300亿美元。消息传出后，软银ADR单日暴跌近10%至每份14.72美元。孙正义已将安保服务定位为检验旗下投资组合公司机器人技术的关键试验场。 Meta发布8160亿参数开放权重模型 ，Muse Spark Open支持100万Token上下文窗口，实际激活参数420亿，主攻编程与智能体任务，采用Muse Model License授权。Meta称其为迄今美国能力最强的开放权重模型，但能力不及本周一推出的闭源Muse Wonder系列。Meta同时与苹果合作，让模型可在两台Mac Studio上运行。 - 苹果和Meta和好了，是AI逼的 ：此前苹果曾因Meta智能体读取Mac私人消息调整系统规则，两周后双方转为合作。 苹果首款折叠屏手机iPhone Duo开启预购 ，10月16日20时开启预售后苹果官网和App被挤崩，10月23日首发日到店取货迅速售罄，邮寄下单发货时间已排到明年1月下旬。该机256GB版本售价15999元，1TB版本21499元。得物App显示多个版本预售成交价突破2万元，1TB黑色版本接近2.9万元，比发售价高出7143元。 - iPhone Duo预购倒计时，京东预约超200万，代抢费炒到888元 ：京东渠道首批商品要求消费者签收时当面激活，闲鱼代抢服务报价300元至1000元不等。 三季度全球智能手机出货量暴跌22% ，IDC初步数据显示当季出货量降至2.553亿部，同比萎缩22.0%，创有纪录以来季度同比最大降幅。存储芯片成本较去年上涨约350%，前五大品牌出货量同比全部下滑，OPPO、vivo降幅均超30%。IDC预计市场增长将持续受限至2027年，复苏至少要推迟到2028年。同期中国大陆智能手机出货量5930万台，同比下滑12%。 CoreWeave三位创始人IPO后套现33亿美元 ，据彭博报道，联合创始人Michael Intrator、Brian Venturo和Brann McBee自2025年3月上市以来累计出售价值33亿美元股票，其中2026年一年套现24亿美元。同期公司五年期信用违约互换利差一度升至1194.5个基点，隐含五年内违约概率超过60%。McBee近40%的个人财富目前以现金及等价物形式持有。 - 危险的信号？CoreWeave三位创始人IPO后套现33亿美元 ：Intrator自年初以来出售逾9.07亿美元，为过去两个季度美国公司五大内部卖家之一。 观点精选 德银 ：AI将把企业切割成采纳者与出局者两类。这份20页报告援引前谷歌CEO施密特的"旧金山共识"，认为超级智能将于2030年前后到来，企业间几乎不存在中间地带。报告援引Epoch数据称，过去三年AI几乎每季度降价一半，相当于每年价格缩减约13倍，算力走完同等降幅耗费了六十年。德银认为传统投资组合管理的三大基石——分散化、以历史波动率衡量风险、下跌时买入——在双峰世界中均可能失效。 桥水 ：本轮利率上行是供给驱动的资本市场再定价。报告指出，利率上行更多反映经济增长超预期韧性与资产供给扩张，而非单纯能源冲击。超大规模云服务商已用尽自身自由现金流，正由向市场提供资金转为从市场获取资金；现代重商主义推动军费与产业政策投入增加，资产净供给规模已接近过去半个世纪高点，需要价格敏感型投资者承接的比例越来越高。 美银Hartnett ：未来数周仍倾向规避风险。美银报告显示，美国股票基金单周吸引390亿美元流入，今年年化流入规模有望达6360亿美元历史新高，科技股以107亿美元流入居首；美国国债连续第16周录得资金流入，创2024年8月以来最长纪录。但Hartnett团队认为，实际收益率上升、AI及银行股价格走势叠加中期选举不确定性，仍支持防御立场。 高盛 ：对冲基金已清空2025年以来AI净买入，逼空燃料充足。数据显示对冲基金连续五个交易日净卖出全球AI股票，2025年以来的净买入头寸被彻底清除，净配置比例从6月峰值31.7%降至26.1%，多空比从4.34降至3.27、处于过去一年第7百分位。全球股票净流量达负2.1个标准差，多头平仓与空头卖出之比约3比1，指向主动降低敞口而非做空押注。 德银 ：黄金量化抛压接近绝对耗尽。金属研究主管Daniel Ghali指出，量化基金风险平价组合的去杠杆规模已达2010年以来完整样本的第90百分位，CTA基金被迫回补约20%的黄金净空头头寸，白银、铂金、钯金分别需增加7%、13%、15%。模拟显示几乎所有价格情景下算法系统目前均偏向买入黄金，但金价需升至约4370美元才能触发下一轮大规模程序化买入。 穆迪分析 ：伊朗战争已给美国家庭带来近2000美元成本。首席经济学家Mark Zandi估算，自2月28日美以对伊朗发动打击以来，综合经济负担约2650亿美元，其中能源与交通成本约1100美元、加息导致的借贷成本约540美元、军事支出分摊约360美元。这笔成本已吞噬美国普通家庭过去八个月收入增幅的约一半。白宫迅速驳斥该测算，并质疑Zandi的立场与过往预测记录。 摩根士丹利 ：AI资本开支暗藏"租赁账单"，2027年投资额上调至1.5万亿美元。该行指出，除自建数据中心外，算力租赁承诺正成为科技巨头表外的重要支出来源，这部分隐性负债使市场对真实资本开支强度的评估偏低。在折旧年限与租赁合同期限错配的情况下，未来的利润压力可能比当前盈利指引所显示的更晚、也更集中地显现。 高盛 ：韩股估值已跌至极低水平，坚守KOSPI 12000点目标。亚太首席股票策略师Tim Moe维持12个月目标位不变，较目前5700点约有110%上涨空间。KOSPI此前连续七个交易日收跌、最大累计跌幅约20%。高盛认为抛压源于三星电子、SK海力士回购买盘退出叠加外资集中减持，外资卖出中约80%至87%集中于这两只存储权重股，属流动性驱动而非需求前景重定价。 澳新数据中心IPO连环折戟，成为全球数据中心债务危机的引线 。英伟达与黑石支持的澳大利亚数据中心运营商Firmus撤回原将成为澳洲史上第二大IPO的上市计划，其寻求的估值达440亿澳元，为三个月前融资估值的两倍，且上市后计划举借最高300亿美元债务。数日后AirTrunk亦取消在新加坡上市REIT的计划。CoreWeave CEO将公司股价下跌部分归咎于此。 今日关注 双11大促进入首个周末，京东、淘天、飞猪等平台活动持续放量，飞猪双11开售4小时活动商品累计销量接近100万件，超200个商家成交额较去年翻倍增长。 美联储自10月17日起进入10月27日至28日议息会议前的静默期，决策者暂停公开发声；沃什16日在曼谷的表态是本轮会议前最后一次公开讲话。 IMF与世界银行年会期间，G20财长与央行行长会议继续举行，全球增长、通胀、利率与政府债务仍是核心议题。 articles.title: 纽约联储调查：服务业提价创2022年来最快，商业活动指数跌至3月来最低
articles.summary: 服务业价格压力正在重新成为美联储政策路径的核心变量。 纽约联储周五发布的最新商业领袖调查显示，10月服务业企业的销售价格涨幅升至2022年以来最快水平，投入成本涨势依然强劲，供应状况持续恶化。 与此同时，企业对商业前景的悲观情绪明显升温，整体商业活动指数较上月下滑12点至负20.7，创3月以来最弱读数。 上述调查结果与当前居高不下的通胀态势相互印证。受特朗普政府关税政策持续冲击以及中东地区冲突推高能源成本等因素影响，价格压力迟迟未能消退。美联储上月已以通胀为由加息，市场普遍预计年内还将再次行动。 服务业价格压力攀升至近三年高位 根据纽约联储最新商业领袖调查，10月服务业企业的销售价格增速加快至2022年以来的最高水平，投入价格涨幅亦保持强劲，供应可及性则持续恶化。 报告还指出，受访企业对当前营商环境的评价"远低于正常水平"，资本支出计划疲软，企业对未来前景趋于悲观。 这一结果与政府同期发布的数据形成共鸣——9月进口价格月率涨幅达1.1%，远超市场预期，再度印证通胀压力并未实质性缓解。 值得注意的是，此次调查所反映的悲观情绪与其他宏观数据之间存在明显分歧。当前美国整体经济活动仍保持强劲，失业率低位稳定，与科技行业相关的投资需求亦维持旺盛态势。 同在纽约联储体系内，周四发布的10月帝国州制造业调查（Empire State）则呈现截然不同的图景——整体商业状况指数升至近五年高位，尽管其中同样伴随着"偏高"的投入和销售价格及供应层面的挑战。 联储官员密切关注服务业通胀 在政策层面，美联储官员对服务业通胀持续高企表达了明确关切。 芝加哥联储主席Austan Goolsbee周三在接受采访时表示，当日发布的消费者通胀报告令人"感到沮丧"，并指出"如果拆分各分项来看，服务业通胀几乎没有改善迹象"。他强调，需要对这部分价格压力"保持密切关注，因为它并非真正来自供给冲击"。 美联储主席沃什周四晚间则对未来政策路径刻意保持模糊。他表示："我不会预判会议结果……我不认为现在应该说我在今年剩余会议上可能会采取什么行动。" 尽管如此，鉴于通胀压力推动美联储上月已再度加息，市场对年内再次加息的预期仍较为强烈。 供应压力加剧成新隐忧 除价格外，供应层面的问题同样不容忽视。 纽约联储调查明确指出，服务业企业面临的供应可及性问题正在加剧，且预计这一状况在未来将进一步恶化。 关税政策对供应链的持续扰动，以及中东局势对能源成本的上行推力，共同构成当前通胀压力难以快速消退的重要背景。 对投资者而言，服务业通胀的顽固性意味着美联储政策转向的时间表存在进一步推迟的风险，利率敏感型资产或将持续承压。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 美国9月进口价格涨幅超预期，核心进口与资本品齐升印证通胀扩散
articles.summary: 美国9月进口价格涨幅超预期，同比升幅创四年多来最高，与本周早些时候公布的消费者及生产者价格数据共同印证通胀压力正全面扩散。 美国劳工部周五公布数据显示，9月进口价格环比上涨1.1%，高于市场预期的0.8%；截至9月的12个月内，进口价格同比上涨8.1%，创2022年7月以来最大涨幅。能源产品价格反弹是主要推手，资本品、消费品价格亦全线走高。 至此，本周美国通胀数据悉数出炉，消费者价格、生产者价格与进口价格均强于预期，令市场对通胀已超出能源领域、向更广泛经济层面蔓延的判断趋于一致。 尽管如此，金融市场目前仍预期美联储将在本月例会上暂停加息，并于12月重启紧缩。 通胀压力多点爆发，特朗普政策被指是主因 本次进口价格报告与本周消费者及生产者价格数据相互印证，共同勾勒出一幅通胀全面升温的图景。 经济学家将通胀加速归因于特朗普政府的关税政策及旷日持久的美以对伊战争——后者扰乱了供应链，并持续推高油价。路透社与益普索的联合民调亦显示， 约78%的美国人认为特朗普政策是生活成本上升的主要原因。 FWDBONDS首席经济学家Christopher Rupkey表示： "美国人在每一个层面都面临通胀威胁，无论转向何处，都不得不为同样的商品多掏钱，而这些商品在几个月前还更便宜。特朗普2.0经济政策在2025年1月开始推出之前，进口商品并不存在通胀，但今年它无处不在。" 能源与资本品价格双双走强 从分项数据来看，能源是拉动9月进口价格的最主要因素。 进口燃料价格环比反弹4.8%，此前8月曾下跌0.2%。 食品价格则维持不变，8月为下跌0.6%。剔除食品和燃料的核心进口价格上涨0.7%，与上月持平，同比涨幅达6.2%。 资本品价格上涨0.9%，与8月涨幅持平，主要受计算机、外围设备及半导体价格上涨驱动——AI投资热潮是背后推手。 工业及服务机械进口成本亦有所上升，抵消了科学及医疗机械价格的回落。 来自日本、欧盟、墨西哥及加拿大的进口价格出现上涨。进口航空旅客票价9月大幅跳升12.6%，但经季节性调整后，该分项对美联储重点跟踪的个人消费支出（PCE）价格指数的影响基本持平。 核心PCE或加速上行，美联储政策路径承压 本次进口价格数据对美联储政策前景具有直接影响。 经济学家对9月核心PCE价格指数环比涨幅的预估集中在0.31%至0.36%区间，四舍五入后可能达到0.4%，对应同比涨幅约3.1%。 8月核心PCE环比上涨0.2%，同比上涨3.0%。 Nationwide金融市场经济学家Oren Klachkin表示："我们预计通胀在短期内将加速，但不会在较高水平上形成平台。话虽如此，风险在于通胀持续高于预期的时间更长，且比美联储预想的更难压制。" 制造业增长但势头放缓，AI效应喜忧参半 美联储同日发布的另一份报告显示，9月工厂产出环比反弹0.3%，8月曾下降0.2%，同比上涨1.1%。企业为满足强劲内需而补充库存，以及AI投资热潮的持续，为制造业提供了支撑。 然而，制造业在三季度整体明显失速，折年率仅增长0.7%，较二季度5.6%的增速大幅回落。半导体及相关电子元件产量三季度飙升28.4%，但汽车及零部件产量9月下降3.0%，三季度折年率萎缩3.4%。 花旗集团经济学家Veronica Clark指出："尽管AI需求的强劲拉动了商业投资，但其中大部分投资属于进口，这意味着国内生产的受益程度并不如表面数据那般显著。" 9月制造业产能利用率从8月的75.8%微升至75.9%，仍低于长期平均水平2.3个百分点。BMO资本市场高级经济学家Sal Guatieri据此判断，生产商或有一定空间消化部分能源及其他投入成本上涨，但并非全部——本周偏热的消费者及生产者价格报告已对此有所印证。 在AI相关行业之外，高企的能源价格、与加拿大之间的贸易摩擦、借贷成本上升以及税收激励刺激效果的消退，均对制造业构成下行风险。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 美芯片股八连跌！2万亿美元市值蒸发，创2008年来最长跌势
articles.summary: 一场围绕人工智能投资回报前景的市场质疑将 芯片股推入八连跌困境 ， 创下2008年金融危机以来最长连跌纪录 。 本周纳指累跌超4%、创2025年4月关税动荡以来最差单周表现。费城半导体指数本周累跌11.4%，过去八个交易日累计下跌逾13%、蒸发市值约2万亿美元。 AI基础设施建设成本高企、而企业盈利回报前景模糊，正令投资者重新审视这一赛道的逻辑根基。嘉盛分析师Fawad Razaqzada表示： 本周的价格走势表明，市场辩论的焦点开始转移。问题不再是AI的市场空间有多大，而是实现这一目标所需的巨额投入最终能有多少盈利。 美国银行的Michael Hartnett警告称，未来数周市场将以规避风险为主基调，投资者正寻求回避AI交易、高利率环境及美国中期选举带来的不确定性。 芯片股连跌纪录，2万亿美元市值蒸发 费城半导体指数本周累跌11.4%，连续下跌八个交易日，创2008年金融危机以来最长连跌纪录，这也是该指数今年内第五次出现至少10%的回调。 据Stocktwits，半导体股票市值过去八连跌已蒸发约2万亿美元。若以各股较自身52周高点的跌幅计算，整个半导体板块损失市值约达4万亿美元。尽管如此，费城半导体指数年内至今仍累涨约60%。 周五追踪该指数的ETF（SOXQ）大幅下挫近4%，Stocktwits平台上散户对SOXQ的情绪在过去一天内由"中性"降至"看跌"。 跌幅波及范围广泛。指数第一大权重股 英伟达 单周下挫超6%；半导体设备制造商 应用材料 和 科天半导体 回撤幅度更深，显示抛压并非仅局限于芯片设计环节。 存储芯片领域同样承压， 美光 本周大幅下跌14.6%， 存储芯片指数 本周累跌17.6%。 CoreWeave成关注焦点，高息债务模式遭质疑 本轮抛售中，CoreWeave因其高度依赖高收益债市场为AI基础设施扩张融资，而成为市场关注的核心标的。 周五美股云计算服务商CoreWeave再跌11.9%，本周累计暴跌超25%。周五其债券已跌至通常预示财务困境的水平，折射出市场对高收益债务融资模式的深层担忧。 据彭博社，以超大规模云服务商为代表的科技巨头资本支出正逼近每年1万亿美元，其中相当比例依赖债务融资。在美国国债收益率高企、10年期美债收益率已升至5.09%的背景下，融资成本持续攀升。 Fawad Razaqzada指出： 较高的利率一方面压低了未来现金流的现值，另一方面又抬升了支撑AI下一阶段增长所需基础设施的融资成本，这对AI交易构成双重不利。 他同时表示，相关担忧已开始向信贷市场蔓延。 ARK创始人“木头姐”Cathie Wood对此持不同看法。 她将CoreWeave与Coinbase类比，认为后者债券在加密行业爆发前也曾承压，但最终受益于行业成长。 她表示，ARK本周在下跌期间增持了CoreWeave及Cerebras。 英伟达CEO持乐观立场，策略师提示反弹风险 面对本轮股价下跌，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在柏林的一场活动中向彭博记者Emily Chang表示，AI技术的收益很快将超越投资者的担忧。 黄仁勋说： 这一切都会过去，原因很简单，它将是变革性的，将以积极的方式影响每一个行业和每一个国家，毫无疑问，这将持续下去，而我们现在只是处于起点。 市场策略师则提示投资者不应过度看空。SpotGamma的Brett Pachuba在接受CNBC采访时表示， 若Meta或谷歌等大型科技公司发布正面消息，可能重新点燃市场对AI股的需求，届时仓位不足的投资者将面临踏空风险。 他表示： 我确实认为，当投资者逐渐转入看跌模式时，需要格外警惕。 Roundhill Investments首席执行官Dave Maza则指出，存储芯片股的投资者情绪已转负，原因涉及产业链竞争压力、博通CEO Hock Tan的公开表态以及宏观经济挑战。 不过他同时强调，存储芯片实际需求依然强劲，供货已售罄至2027年，客户需求甚至延伸至2028年。Annex的Brian Jacobsen则表示： 本周最值得关注的事件，不是通胀数据或美联储的表态，而是市场的反应方式。当多只AI相关股票回调时，资金流向了医疗、金融、材料以及中小市值公司，这些板块表现相对较好。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 人工智能基础设施热潮遭遇投资者信心考验之际，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋公开为AI前景背书，呼吁市场聚焦长期基本面。 黄仁勋周四在柏林接受彭博采访时表示， 眼下市场动荡"终将过去"，原因在于AI技术具有变革性，将对每一个行业和每一个国家产生积极影响。他强调，这一进程仍处于起点，不会因短期波动而改变。 这番表态发布于费城半导体指数连续第八个交易日下跌之际，此轮下跌势头为2008年以来最长连跌纪录，英伟达自身股价在过去八个交易日中亦有七日录得跌幅。 AI基础设施建设的代表性企业CoreWeave本周首当其冲，股价单周重挫逾四分之一，其公司债券价格亦跌至通常预示财务困境的水平。英伟达是CoreWeave的主要股东之一。 市场动荡难撼AI基本面判断 黄仁勋在采访中对当前的市场环境保持乐观立场。 "一些消息面确实嘈杂，"他说，"新闻每天都在发生，但这不会改变基本面。" 他预计，企业对AI硬件的大规模投入最终将产生可观回报，从而逐步消解市场的不安情绪。在他看来，当前投资者所担忧的AI支出可持续性问题，将随技术价值的兑现而化解。 黄仁勋多次敦促投资者超越短期报告的视野，将注意力集中于技术的长期价值。 "回归第一性原理，聚焦基本面，"他在采访中再度强调。 芯片股承压，CoreWeave遭受重创 此轮抛售波及整个芯片及AI基础设施板块。费城半导体指数已连跌八个交易日，创下自2008年金融危机以来最长跌势；英伟达股价在过去八个交易日中七度收跌。 压力集中体现在云计算服务商CoreWeave身上。该公司股价本周跌幅达四分之一，其公司债券亦跌至通常被市场视为困境信号的价格区间。英伟达作为CoreWeave的重要支持方之一，持有后者股份。 此轮市场调整的背景是，投资者对借贷成本持续偏高环境下AI支出能否维系产生疑虑，对相关企业的盈利路径愈发审慎。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 首场简报会表现糟糕，特朗普考虑更换白宫新闻秘书人选
articles.summary: △凯蒂·扎卡里亚 当地时间10月16日，美国总统特朗普表示，也许白宫新闻秘书这一职位并不适合凯蒂·扎卡里亚。他会与扎卡里亚谈谈。特朗普称，已告诉扎卡里亚应该重新考虑这一职位。 白宫官员透露，凯蒂·扎卡里亚正着手卸任特朗普新闻秘书一职。另有三位知情人士透露，扎卡里亚于当日被解职，此时她上任还不到一周。但白宫和扎卡里亚本人均未回应置评请求。 上一任白宫新闻秘书莱维特8月底离职后，这一职位一直空缺。特朗普当地时间10月9日宣布任命保守派评论员扎卡里亚出任白宫新闻秘书。扎卡里亚此前是特朗普媒体科技集团旗下“真实社交”网站的高级通讯顾问，还曾任国土安全部发言人兼公共事务副助理部长，经常在福克斯新闻频道等保守派媒体担任评论员。不过，扎卡里亚10月13日的首场白宫简报会表现糟糕，还被指履历造假，引发人们对其能力的质疑。 本文来源： 央视新闻 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
